newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea wet crude holds firm, Iraq spot barrels trade.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea wet crude holds firm, Iraq spot barrels trade.

text.p: The North Sea wet crude market held firm on Thursday although action waned after two early Brent deals.

Weakening CFD values signalled a softening of wet Brent values from strong traded levels, but traders said that the North Sea market was in general well supported after brisk trade in the last couple of days cleared out a lot of March barrels.
Two Brent cargoes loading March 14-16 traded this morning at April Brent +55 cents.
The buyer now holds some eight cargoes and was heard to be working two VLCCs to South Africa.
Traders said that the buyer was keen to bid the market up to support a long swaps position.
"But the market looks in good shape. You can't bid a weak market up, but you can accentuate it if you want to go in a certain direction," said one trader.
Prompt CFDs failed to match the levels seen in the wet market, but next week's dates (March 3-7) traded at a high of April Brent +29 cents.
But in afternoon talk CFD values shed more than 10 cents with March 3-7 trading at April Brent +18 cents and March 10-14 at April +5.
Outright April Brent paper slipped to talk around $19.50/ $19.55 a barrel in line with the IPE screen, having traded earlier at $19.70. The April/May spread traded at +33 cents.
Other North sea grades were quiet. An Ekofisk loading March 26-28 traded some five cents firmer at dated Brent +29 cents.

In the Mediterranean, an end-Feb loading Iraqi Kirkuk cargo was sold into Portugal. The seller declined to comment on the price but traders said it appeared well above the Dated Brent -$2 a barrel assessed by some players.
Another cargo bought by a trader from Hungarian refiner MOL was heard resold into Romania, again at an undisclosed level.
